column3: The Hebrew says he arose and they built the Sheep Gate; BSB says they began rebuilding there. The final dedication has an unnamed object in Hebrew; BSB identifies it as the wall.
The Hebrew twice says “at his hand”; BSB names Eliashib first and then uses the plural “them.”
The Hebrew makes the sons of Hassenaah the active builders; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew repeatedly says “at their hand,” using plural possessors; BSB twice uses the singular “him.”
The Hebrew pictures their refusal as not bringing their neck into the service of their lords; BSB uses shoulders and work under supervisors.
The Hebrew makes Joiada and Meshullam the active repairers; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew uses an active repairing verb and mentions the governor’s throne; BSB uses a passive and says they were under his authority. It names Beyond the River; BSB specifies west of the Euphrates.
The Hebrew says “at his hand” initially and describes Hananiah as son of the perfumers, plural; BSB says “next to them” initially and son of the perfumer, singular.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew initially says “at their hand”; BSB says “next to him.”
The Hebrew says a second section; BSB says another section.
The Hebrew says “at his hand” and “he and his daughters”; BSB says “next to them” and describes the daughters as helping him. It does not explicitly say “other” half-district in Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes Hanun and the residents the active repairers; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew makes Malchijah the active repairer; BSB uses the passive.
The Hebrew makes Shallun the active repairer; BSB uses the passive.

The Hebrew names Rehum after the Levites without an explicit word for “under,” which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew names Bavvai and calls them their brothers; BSB names Binnui and says countrymen. It does not explicitly say “other” half-district in Hebrew.
The Hebrew says a second section; BSB says another section.
The Hebrew names Zakkai; BSB names Zabbai. It says a second section, where BSB says another section.
The Hebrew repeats “the house of Eliashib”; BSB shortens the second occurrence to “the house.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew twice says “after him,” singular; BSB uses “them,” plural.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls it the upper house of the king; BSB says the upper palace.
The Hebrew says the temple servants were dwelling on Ophel without an explicit repair verb here; BSB says they made repairs and explicitly identifies Ophel as a hill.
The Hebrew says “after him” and a second section; BSB says “next to them” and another section.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew initially says “after him”; BSB says “next to them.”
The Hebrew calls his room a chamber and says “after him”; BSB says quarters and “next to them.”
